correctness.rationale: For prime p, each interior binomial C(p,k),C(p,k−1) has p-adic valuation one, so Narayana N(p,k)=C(p,k)C(p,k−1)/p has exactly one p. Since N(p,2)=p(p−1)/2, any additional common prime must divide p−1. For any odd ℓ|p−1, take k=ℓ^{vℓ(p−1)}+1; Lucas's theorem makes both binomials nonzero mod ℓ; likewise ℓ=2 when p−1 has an odd factor. If p−1=2^r, direct 2-adic valuation N(p,k) for k≥3 equals 2r−v2(k)−2v2(k−1)−v2(k−2), with k=2 giving r−1; parity bounds and explicit sharp witnesses give min{2,r−1}. All odd prime cases including p=3 and p=5 are handled. Independent Python exact gcd of every row for 96 odd primes p≤509 agreed; finite checks alone are not the unrestricted argument.

originality.rationale: Bóna–Sagan (2005), inspected in full, establishes p-divisibility of every interior Narayana number for n=p^m, but not the entire gcd, exact absence of other prime factors, or extra binary factors at Fermat primes. Resultary searches of Narayana row valuations, parity and gcd classification found no published theorem implying this exact all-odd-prime row content. This exact minimization requires Lucas witnesses and valuation optimization. The potentially relevant Eu–Liu–Yeh (2006) complete paper was not accessible; its abstract alone cannot establish noncoverage, so the priority risk is expressly retained, not used as a scientific failure.

value.rationale: The interior-row gcd is the maximal common modulus of all nontrivial Dyck path peak enumerators at prime semilength. A full all-prime classification with a sharp and rare Fermat-prime binary exception materially strengthens known prime divisibility and is a useful natural exact arithmetic invariant. Lucas nondivisibility witnesses and exact 2-adic minimization go beyond textbook substitution, despite being a bounded prime-row family.

final_claim: For every odd prime p, the gcd of all nonendpoint Narayana entries N(p,k), 2≤k≤p−1, equals p except for Fermat primes p=2^r+1, where it equals p·2^{min(2,r−1)} (3→3, 5→10, Fermat primes ≥17→4p).
limitations: Only odd-prime Narayana rows and nonendpoint entries; composite rows and existence of further Fermat primes are not asserted. Eu–Liu–Yeh full text inaccessible (institutional VPN disconnected); its possible coverage remains a priority risk, not a scientific failure.
